summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. K.H.
key_cases.holding: The Court reinstated a termination judgment, holding that substantial evidence supported the family court's findings and that the reasonable-efforts inquiry under KRS 625.090(3)(c) is confined to the Cabinet's efforts before the termination petition was filed, regardless of when the permanency goal changed.
key_cases.relevance: It defines how a court measures whether the Cabinet genuinely tried to reunify before abandoning that goal.
key_cases.quote: KRS 625.090(3)(c) focuses only on the Cabinet's efforts prior to the TPR petition, irrespective of the permanency goals

key_cases.case_name: Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. C.V.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of the Cabinet's termination petition because the circuit court made no findings that would support termination, while agreeing with the Cabinet that a district-court change of the permanency goal from reunification to adoption is not a prerequisite to filing a termination petition.
key_cases.relevance: The trial court's conditional dismissal preserved reunification as the goal so long as the parents met their plan obligations.
key_cases.quote: Under KRS 625.090(3)(c), the court can make its own concurrent finding as to reasonable efforts

key_cases.case_name: Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. J.M.G.
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed criminal contempt sanctions imposed on the Cabinet for missing a KRS 620.240 case-progress report and an FCRPP 34 pretrial date because willfulness was not proved, but it recognized that the family court had ample justification for finding that the Cabinet's delay was a failure to make reasonable efforts to finalize the children's permanency plan.
key_cases.relevance: It addresses the conflict between caseworkers waiting out incarcerated parents for reunification and a court order to prepare the children for adoption.
key_cases.quote: the trial court had ample justification for finding that the Cabinet's foot dragging amounted to at least a lack of due diligence and a failure to make reasonable efforts

key_cases.case_name: D.G.R. v. Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The Court reinstated a trial court's refusal to terminate parental rights, holding that only a decision to terminate must rest on clear and convincing evidence, that parents may defeat termination by showing by a preponderance that the child will not be abused in the future, and that the KRS 625.090(3) best-interest factors are to be considered rather than treated as a checklist.
key_cases.relevance: It recognizes the parents' statutory right under KRS 625.090(5) to defeat termination by proving the child will not be abused going forward, preserving a reunification path.
key_cases.quote: the Cabinet must prove the necessary statutory allegations by clear and convincing evidence in order for the trial court to terminate parental rights

key_cases.holding: The court held that a permanent custody award may be entered within a KRS Chapter 620 dependency action if the proper procedures are followed, but reversed because the family court failed to make sufficient findings on the KRS 403.270 best-interest factors and did not account for the mother's progress on her case plan.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion protects a parent who has completed case-plan tasks from losing her children permanently without findings that address that progress.
key_cases.quote: such a hearing and an award of custody are not precluded by the structure of KRS Chapter 620, so long as the proper procedures are followed
